text: Categories: case-insensitive merge, central casing fix, drop web uppercase, web category autocomplete

CASING-CORRECTION UX SETTLED — two entry points, one shared operation.

Shared operation ("canonicalize category X to string Y"): rewrite every item whose
`lower(category) == lower(X)` to Y, AND update X's `category_order` entry to Y
(casing + keep position). Both entry points below call this; only the trigger and
the gate differ. Both clients implement it identically.

1. ITEM EDIT DIALOG (long-press item on Android / open on web), editing the
   category field:
   - SAME word, different casing (`lower(new)==lower(old)`, `new!=old`) → run the
     shared op: recase ALL items in that category. Rationale: recasing a single
     item is a no-op under case-insensitive grouping, so "fix the whole category's
     casing" is the only meaningful interpretation.
   - DIFFERENT word (`lower(new)!=lower(old)`) → normal re-categorize of THIS one
     item only.
   - Show a toast on the recase-all ("Fixed casing for N items in Y"); it's
     non-destructive and reversible by re-editing. (Chosen over an explicit
     scope prompt.)
   - Accepted footgun: a different-word edit here moves only the one item, so a
     whole-category WORD rename can't be done from the item dialog (it would split
     the category). That's the correct default — "re-categorize this item" is the
     common case — but it means full renames go through list settings.

2. LIST SETTINGS → category entry: full rename (ANY change) → runs the shared op on
   the whole category. This is where you rename to a different word. The panel
   shows the FULL category set (in-use ∪ ordered) so any category is reachable;
   a rename whose target collides case-insensitively with another category MERGES
   them — confirm ("this will merge into Y").

Spec line in client-ui-notes.md defines the gate + shared op as the single source
of truth so the two clients can't drift.
